title: Pydantic is all you need: Jason Liu
talk_summary: Jason Liu argues that defining Pydantic models as the interface to LLM calls (structured prompting) replaces fragile string/JSON parsing with typed, validated, reviewable code. He shows Instructor's pattern of response_model + validation + max_retries, plus design patterns like escape-hatch objects, reusable components with optional chain-of-thought fields, and validators that enforce business rules (e.g. quote-must-exist-in-source) instead of asking the model not to hallucinate.

takeaways.technique: Typed response schemas with validation + retry loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Define a Pydantic model as the response_model; on validation failure, capture all errors in one shot, append them to the conversation, and re-ask the model up to max_retries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can also capture all the validations in one shot send it back to the language model and try again

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of instructing the model to say 'I don't know' in caps and string-matching it, model the output as an object with an optional result plus an explicit error field, so 'not found' is a first-class typed outcome.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's really important for us to give language models the ability to have an escape hatch and say that it doesn't know something

takeaways.technique: Validator-enforced grounding (quote must exist in source)
takeaways.what_they_do: Model answers as facts each carrying a substring quote from the source chunk; a validator drops any fact whose quote isn't literally present, and only facts with at least one verified quote survive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for every quote you give me validate that it exists in the text Chunk if it's not there throw out the fact

takeaways.technique: Optional chain-of-thought field toggled per environment
takeaways.what_they_do: Add a reasoning field inside a reusable component so it can be enabled in testing/debugging and disabled in production to trade latency for accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in production you uh disable that Chain of Thought Field and then in in in testing you add that to figure out what's the latency or performance trade-offs

takeaways.technique: Model plans as a DAG of dependencies
takeaways.what_they_do: Have the model emit a query plan as nodes with IDs and dependency lists, so independent nodes run in parallel and dependent ones wait, replacing an agent for-loop with a classical scheduler.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I could query the first two in parallel because there are no dependencies and then wait for dependency three to merge

takeaways.technique: Reusable typed components as shared contracts
takeaways.what_they_do: Define shared Pydantic components (e.g. TimeRange) reused across prompts so schema, docstrings, and validators are maintained in one place and reviewed like code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your code quality your prompt quality your data quality are all in sync there's this one thing you want to manage
